Softly--oh, soft! let us rest on the oar, And vex not a billow that sighs to the shore:-- For sacred the spot where the starry waves meet With the beach, where the breath of the citron is sweet. There’s a spell on the waves that now waft us along To the last of our Muses, the Spirit of Song.

The Eagle of old renown, And the Lombard’s iron crown And Milan’s mighty name are ours no more; But by this glassy water, Harmonia’s youngest daughter, Still from the lightning saves one laurel to our shore.
